objectives.description: Does not over-block (stash, stash pop, restore --staged, quoted substring)

objectives.note: Confirmed live: this session's own Bash tool call was blocked mid-implementation by the newly-registered hook when it literally contained 'git clean -qfd', proving real enforcement, not just structural presence in settings.json

notes: All testing performed in disposable /tmp git repos or via crafted JSON piped directly to the hook script; no destructive git command was ever run against this actual working tree. Test scripts were written to files and invoked via 'bash <file>' rather than as inline multi-line Bash tool calls, after discovering the live guard-destructive-git.sh hook (now registered in this repo's own .claude/settings.json) intercepts literal destructive-command substrings in ANY submitted Bash tool call, including test harness code -- this was itself confirmation the hook works end-to-end.
